cuts.reason: Cuts from the wide walking shot to the elevator two-shot right as the woman's setup line ('You know what's dark?') lands, resetting the frame for the deadpan 'What?' reply and holding on both characters for the joke's delivery.

Cuts from the static two-shot to a tight push-in on the husband's face immediately after the punchline ('...never admit you were wrong in that parking lot argument'), isolating his reaction for the beat of silence that follows.
Cuts from the husband's blank stunned reaction straight to the black title card, ending the scene on his non-response and letting the joke land without a verbal capper.

reaction_shots.description: Close-up push-in on the husband's face, eyes wide and mouth slightly open, stunned/silent after his wife's dark 'you'll never admit you were wrong' line — the shot exists purely to sell his reaction, not to advance plot.

pacing_notes: The scene opens with two unhurried, similarly long shots (~2.9s and ~5.5s) that carry the setup and the full punchline line via dialogue, giving the joke room to breathe. Once the line lands, pacing tightens sharply into a ~2.8s silent reaction close-up on the husband's face, using the cut itself (not more dialogue) to mark the punchline. The video then closes on a short ~1.1s title card, a quick button that doesn't linger. Overall the rhythm is slow-build-then-snap: long conversational shots leading into an abrupt reaction cut, mirroring the joke's structure of a mundane setup ('what's dark?') flipping into a bleak specific punchline.
